packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 02 - FIRST READING (unverified image reading)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context before this task proposed an identification or reading of these leaves.
- The images themselves carry modern pencil notes: shelfmark labels "Stams, STA, Frg. 84_1r / 84_1v / 84_2r / 84_2v" (bottom margins), "6.IX - S. Magni" (top margin of the 1r leaf), "6.IX" (bottom of 1r), "8.IX" (bottom of 2r and 1v). The note "S. Magni" is a modern proposal visible in the image and I saw it before reading. I report it here. I did not use it to fill gaps.
- The only file I opened apart from PROMPT.md and image-001..026 was an attempted read of image-027.jpg, which does not exist. I tried it only to confirm the image count. I did not list the directory, use the web, or read packet.json.
- All 26 images loaded.

IMAGE MAP (from the overviews)
- image-001 = overview, recto faces. Left leaf labelled "...Frg. 84_2r". Right leaf labelled "...Frg. 84_1r".
- image-014 = overview, verso faces. Left leaf labelled "...84_2v". Right leaf labelled "...84_1v".
- Tiles (they overlap their neighbours):
  2r: col a top 002, mid 006, bottom 010. col b top 003, mid 007, bottom 011.
  1r: col a top 004, mid 008, bottom 012. col b top 005, mid 009, bottom 013.
  2v: col a top 015, mid 019, bottom 023. col b top 016, mid 020, bottom 024.
  1v: col a top 017, mid 021, bottom 025. col b top 018, mid 022, bottom 026.
Line numbers below count from the top of the named tile. Where tiles overlap, I give each line once, under the tile where it reads best, and say where the overlap starts.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two separate paper(?) leaves. Each face has 2 columns, about 37-39 lines, with dry-point/plummet ruling and a wide lower margin. Script is a small, compressed gothic book hand in brown ink.
- Rubrication in red: abbreviations "R" (with a stroke), "V" (with a stroke), "An" with an overline, "Ps", "Cap", "Euan", "Inuit", "Ymnus"/"ymnus", "lc vi". Also red headings: "In iii noct", "In ii° nocturno", "In iii° no", "Ad laudes", "Ad horas", "In natiuitate beate virginis marie", "Secundum Matheum". Many initials have red touching (a vertical red stroke in the letter). Enlarged red initials: V (2r a), O (2r b), V (2r b bottom), P/D (1r a top), Q/S? (1r a), B (1r a), H (1r b), F (1r b), V (2v a, twice), L (2v b), O/Q (1v a), large decorated S (1v b).
- Tentative interpretation: liturgical office text. Lessons alternate with responsories, versicles, antiphons and psalm incipits. Some lessons are biblical (Song-of-Songs-type wording on 2r/2v). Others are narrative hagiography (1r/1v). The 1v col b marks a change of office ("In natiuitate beate virginis marie"). I make no claim about date or provenance.
- Short faint red/brown cue-dashes appear in the outer margins at many line ends (ruling or catchmarks). No glosses.

SELECTION
I read every face end to end where I could. Each column was read in its own pass. Weakest areas: tops of 2r col a and 1r col b (faded and smudged); the lower part of 2r col a (a large abrasion/stain at lines 10.6-10.12); the faded responsory lines on 2r col b and 2v col b. In these places I leave gaps rather than guess. Higher-contrast or raking-light crops of 2r a lines 1-8 (tile 002) and 1r b lines 1-7 (tile 005) would help.

CONVENTIONS: [red ...] = red ink. "|" marks a red-touched initial when I mention it. Expansions are in (), uncertain readings have (?), and unreadable text is [illegible]. Line breaks are physical.
